question: What is the main job of an information system in a hospital or clinic?

options.A: To manufacture medical equipment for ward use
options.B: To collect, process, and distribute patient information
options.C: To manage hospital financial accounts and budgets only
options.D: To completely replace the need for nursing personnel

explanation: You got this! Hospital information systems are built to gather and share patient data smoothly so that the care team can communicate and work effectively. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h1)

question: How do digital health records make daily nursing handovers easier?

options.A: By shortening the total duration of the shift to two hours
options.B: By providing real-time and legible patient data updates
options.C: By eliminating the need for verbal communication entirely
options.D: By preventing patients from asking questions about treatment

explanation: Great job! No more struggling to read messy handwriting. Digital records ensure your handover notes are clear, updated, and ready when you need them. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of an Electronic Health Record (EHR)?

options.A: A strict financial auditing tool for hospital management
options.B: A public social media platform for healthcare workers
options.C: A personal storage device for physician private documents
options.D: A digital repository for comprehensive patient medical history

explanation: Spot on! An EHR is essentially a patient's complete medical story kept safely online so authorized healthcare workers can view it. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h2)

question: Why is it helpful when different departments can access the same EHR at the same time?

options.A: Physical paper charts become completely unnecessary for billing departments
options.B: Clinicians in different units can view the same updated data simultaneously
options.C: Hospital management can monitor the exact movements of nurses on duty
options.D: Patients can update their own laboratory results from home without approval

explanation: Exactly! When multiple care units can see lab results and notes instantly, patient care flows much faster and safer. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h2)

question: What does a Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) mainly do for nurses and doctors?

options.A: To schedule nursing shifts and calculate monthly salary wages
options.B: To order hospital supplies automatically when stock runs low
options.C: To provide automated alerts and evidence-based recommendations to clinicians
options.D: To make final independent medical diagnoses without human input

explanation: Well done! A CDSS acts like a smart assistant, popping up with helpful reminders and warnings to keep patient care safe. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h3)

question: What should you do as a nurse if the computer pops up with an unexpected medication allergy warning?

options.A: Evaluate the patient's record and verify the allergy before administering
options.B: Cancel the patient's admission immediately without notifying the doctor
options.C: Administer the medication quickly to avoid delaying the treatment schedule
options.D: Ignore the alert because computer software is frequently incorrect

explanation: Safety first! Technology is a great helper, but as a nurse, you always use your critical thinking to double-check alerts before giving meds. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which technology helps stop medication errors caused by messy handwritten prescriptions?
explanation: Correct! Computerized Provider Order Entry (CPOE) lets doctors type orders directly into the system, completely skipping confusing handwriting. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h4)

question: What is the main safety benefit of using a smart infusion pump for IV medications?

options.A: It stops programming that exceeds safe dosage limits
options.B: It removes the requirement to check patient identification bands
options.C: It automatically diagnoses the patient's underlying illness
options.D: It mixes the intravenous fluids without human assistance

explanation: You got it! Smart pumps have built-in safety limits that block dangerous drug doses before they can be pumped into the patient. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h4)

question: What is the main goal of telehealth in healthcare?

options.A: To train nursing students exclusively through video gaming
options.B: To conduct laboratory blood tests without using needles
options.C: To deliver clinical services and consultations across geographic distances
options.D: To replace physical hospitals with entirely automated buildings

explanation: Spot on! Telehealth bridges the gap, allowing patients and health workers to connect across physical distances using technology. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h5)

question: How do nurses use Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) data for patients with long-term illnesses?

options.A: To monitor hospital electrical power consumption in patient rooms
options.B: To diagnose new surgical conditions without a physical exam
options.C: To track physiological readings and catch abnormal trends early
options.D: To replace monthly clinic visits with permanent home isolation

explanation: Well done! RPM lets you keep an eye on vital signs from afar so you can catch small changes before they turn into emergencies. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h5)

question: Which of these actions directly breaks digital patient data security rules?

options.A: Logging out of the electronic health record after a shift
options.B: Asking a system administrator to reset a forgotten password
options.C: Sharing active login passwords with a colleague on the ward
options.D: Locking the computer screen when stepping away from the desk

explanation: Correct! Your login password is your digital signature. Sharing it compromises patient privacy and security audit trails. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why is strict data privacy so important in electronic health systems?

options.A: To prevent nursing students from learning about disease pathologies
options.B: To maintain patient trust and prevent unauthorized disclosure of sensitive health facts
options.C: To make it difficult for doctors to find patient test results quickly
options.D: To ensure that hospital administrators can read personal text messages

explanation: You got it! Keeping patient records private protects their dignity and honors our professional duty of confidentiality. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h6)

question: What is a common challenge when a hospital tries to introduce new health technology?

options.A: The complete absence of any medical software options
options.B: Technophobia and resistance among staff members
options.C: An excess of stable electricity and reliable internet
options.D: Too many nurses who understand software programming

explanation: Spot on! Change can be tough, and fear or hesitation about new software is a very common hurdle on the wards. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h7)

question: Why should frontline nurses be involved when choosing new clinical software?

options.A: They understand daily workflows and can help ensure the system is practical
options.B: They control the financial budget allocated for hospital projects
options.C: They are required by law to write the underlying computer code
options.D: They are the only staff members allowed to operate computer hardware

explanation: Brilliant! Since nurses use the system daily, involving them ensures the technology actually works well in a busy clinical setting. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h7)
